analysis_md:
# LULU — lululemon athletica inc.
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-19 (engine 5.5.0). In scope: market cap $11.640B at $97.76 (nasdaq_quote_api), under the $40B scope line. Fiscal labels: the engine, the CSV and statements.json name a fiscal year by its end date, so the annual period ended 2026-02-01 is FY2026 in those outputs; the company names that same year fiscal 2025, and its Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-08-02) and the FY2026 guidance quoted below are company fiscal 2026 — the year ending January 2027, i.e. engine FY2027.

All engine figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed. Quarter and guidance figures are from the company's Q2 FY2026 release (filed 2026-09-03, quarter ended 2026-08-02) as reported in search results.

## What it is
Premium athletic apparel ("athleisure") sold direct: 825 company-operated stores at Q2 FY2026 plus digital (~39% of Q2 revenue). Proprietary fabrics (Nulu, Everlux), premium prices, no dividend. Americas is the dominant region (~71% of FY2025 revenue per external analysis); China/international is the growth leg. The business is in a demand reset: Q2 FY2026 revenue fell 4% YoY, comparable sales fell 9%, and management cut full-year guidance hard (below).

## Owner's earnings
**Latest FY (ended 2026-02-01, 10-K filed 2026-03-17, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $11,102,600,000 (+4.86% YoY); operating cash flow $1,602,477,000; capex $680,802,000 (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, rollup — the whole capex line; no intangible purchases filed); SBC $62,203,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings, latest FY: $859,472,000 = $7.22/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $7.22, latest FY OE total $859.5M)
- Maintenance version (same CSV row): $1,167,568,000 — above the conservative figure on its own construction (net income + D&A − capex capped at D&A − delta_nwc); the working-capital build inside the latest FY's OCF is identified line by line under BASE_DIVERGENCE below.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. OE/share by year (CSV): $3.95, $7.10, $1.95, $12.20, $12.05, $7.22 — volatile (see OE_VOLATILE).
- Balance sheet from the filing (fundamentals.json, latest FY): cash $1,807,202,000 on the combined cash + restricted-cash tag; **no funded debt filed** (no debt_current / debt_lt tags — see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK); total liabilities $3,494,903,000, of which operating lease liabilities $1,798,441,000; equity $4,961,840,000; current ratio 2.26. At Q2 FY2026 the company reported cash of $1.39B with $593.7M available under its revolving facility (search-cited call reporting). This is a net-cash retailer whose real fixed obligation is store leases, roughly covered by cash alone.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 FY2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $1,602,477,000 − prior YTD $209,722,000 + current YTD $589,278,000 = **TTM $1,982,033,000**
- Capex: FY $680,802,000 − prior YTD $330,161,000 + current YTD $277,056,000 = **TTM $627,697,000**
- SBC: FY $62,203,000 − prior YTD $21,247,000 + current YTD $50,275,000 = **TTM $91,231,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **114,201,000**
- **TTM OE total $1,263,105,000 → base OE/share $11.06** (base_source: ttm_json; key_numbers.md base OE/share $11.06)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is $12.05/share — reported, not used: it is built from FY2024–FY2026 and two of those years predate the demand break, so it overstates the current run-rate (see BASE_DIVERGENCE).
- **One-off inside the TTM base:** Q2 FY2026 results include $134.5M of IEEPA tariff refunds (plus $4.1M associated interest) that added $0.86/share to Q2 diluted EPS and 560bp to Q2 gross margin (company release, search-cited). That refund sits inside TTM operating cash flow. Rather than a base_override (the refund figure is not printed in this run's engine outputs, so a filing/estimate construction under step 8(c) is not available), the scenarios strip it through the OE multipliers: the base-case multiplier is 0.90 instead of 1.00, which removes $126,310,500 of the $134.5M refund from the $1,263,105,000 of TTM OE (an exact strip would take a 0.8935 multiplier). The ladder uses round steps, so a residual of $8,189,500 — 0.65% of TTM OE — stays in the base case; counting the $4.1M interest as part of the one-off as well, the residual is $12,289,500, still under 1% of TTM OE and not tier-relevant. The bear ladder runs 0.70 / 0.80 below that step. The bull case at 1.00 is the refund-inclusive TTM level sustained — deliberately the optimistic end.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow, and eroding
Evidence first (fundamentals.json): ROIC proxy over the last six fiscal years ran 41.9% / 65.9% / 42.7% / 76.4% / 75.4% / 49.4% — far above any plausible cost of capital through a cycle that included COVID and the FY2023 inventory glut. Gross margin: 56.0% / 57.7% / 55.4% / 58.3% / 59.2% / 56.6% over the same years; TTM gross margin 56.1%. Those are wide-moat economics historically. The score is 5, not 7–8, because the pillars producing those returns are visibly weakening now (AGAINST, below) and a moat score must price the franchise the buyer gets today.
- FOR: proprietary technical fabrics (Nulu, Everlux) and a fit reputation that still supports premium pricing — gross margin held at 56.6% in the latest FY even as demand fell; returns on capital far above cost of capital through a full cycle (ROIC series above); direct-to-consumer model — stores plus digital, no wholesale channel to discount against it; international revenue still growing (+4% in Q2 FY2026, constant-dollar +2%) while Americas fell; net-cash balance sheet funds a turnaround internally.
- AGAINST: the core market is shrinking under it — Americas comparable sales −12% and Americas revenue −8% in Q2 FY2026, with core leggings sales down ~20% as silhouettes shifted to looser fits the franchise was late to; Alo Yoga and Vuori are running lululemon's own community playbook at the same premium price band — reported US athleisure share down ~10pp to 43.9%; product execution failures (the pulled "Get Low" leggings) and a China brand-sentiment backlash (Great Wall campaign) damage exactly the fit/quality reputation the premium rests on; leadership is in transition — CEO departed, interim co-CEOs through 2026, a founder (Chip Wilson) proxy fight, and incoming CEO Heidi O'Neill (Nike veteran) arriving with an unproven plan; the product is premium discretionary — the first category consumers defer — with no cost advantage underneath the brand if the brand fades.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
**Growth sanity check (mandatory):** the engine's blended growth is 10.31% (components, key_numbers.md: revenue CAGR 5y 20.32%, 3y 11.00%, latest revenue YoY 4.86%, OE/share CAGR 2y −22.97%). Every one of the revenue components is a backward-looking average that straddles the demand break. The actual current prints are: Q2 FY2026 revenue −4% YoY with comparable sales −9%; Q3 FY2026 guidance of revenue down 10–11%; full-year FY2026 guidance (company naming; engine FY2027) cut to $10.35–$10.50B, a decline of 5–7% versus the latest FY, with diluted EPS guided to $9.48–$9.73 *including* the $0.86 tariff-refund benefit. Running the default starts (base +10.3%, bull +15.3%, super bull +22.3%) would have every scenario — including the bear cases — assume growth the company just guided *against*; the preliminary run on those defaults printed Tier A at a 20.46% weighted IRR, which is an artifact of the stale blend, not a finding. Scenario starts were therefore set directly from the prints and guidance via offsets (−0.183 / −0.143 / −0.103 / −0.053 / −0.003 against the 10.31% blend): super bear −8.0%, bear −4.0%, base 0.0% (a flat start that only converges up to the 2.5% terminal rate over the CAP — i.e., stabilization under the new CEO, not a return to compounding), bull +5.0%, super bull +10.0% (a genuine brand recovery; still below the company's own 3-yr revenue CAGR of 11.00%). Probabilities were shifted bearish from the 10/25/30/25/10 default to 15/30/30/18/7 — 45% on bear-or-worse — per OE_VOLATILE and the guidance reset. OE multipliers 0.70 / 0.80 / 0.90 / 1.00 / 1.10 (base 0.90 strips ~94% of the tariff-refund one-off from the TTM base, above). Price $97.76.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -8.0% | 0.70 | Brand fade compounds; Alo/Vuori take the core customer; declines persist | $40.91 | 7.27% |
| Bear | 30% | -4.0% | 0.80 | Guidance-level declines, then stagnation; no real recovery under new leadership | $55.31 | 9.31% |
| Base | 30% | 0.0% | 0.90 | Declines stop; flat OE (refund-stripped base, 0.90 multiplier) converging to terminal growth over the CAP | $73.57 | 11.84% |
| Bull | 18% | 5.0% | 1.00 | O'Neill product reset works; Americas stabilize, international carries growth | $100.67 | 15.36% |
| Super bull | 7% | 10.0% | 1.10 | Full franchise recovery toward historical growth | $136.15 | 19.48% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $72.45 (−25.9% vs price), IV@12% $94.89 (−2.9%), IV@10% $119.78, weighted IRR 11.72%, base-case IRR 11.84%**
- **Tier by numbers: C.** Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path, key_numbers.md): clears 15% at $72.45, 20% at $52.09, 25% at $40.73. Diagnostics: OE yield 11.31%, terminal value 17.4% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.33x, 8.5 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 8.5 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through the Q2 FY2026 quarter ended 2026-08-02, legs quoted above. Note the TTM window still ends before the September guidance reset; the scenarios, not the base, carry that news.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share $7.22 vs 3-yr median $12.05): both are distorted, in opposite directions. The latest FY is depressed by a working-capital build that the filing's balance sheet identifies line by line (statements.json): inventories rose $258,672,000 in FY2026 ($1,442,081,000 → $1,700,753,000, +17.9% against revenue growth of +4.86%) and receivables rose $70,484,000 ($120,173,000 → $190,657,000), partly offset by accounts payable +$60,015,000 and accrued liabilities +$103,519,000, while income taxes payable fell $139,178,000. In the engine's own series the same build is the delta_nwc swing in financials_history.csv — from −$29,009,000 in FY2025 to +$411,615,000 in FY2026, a $440,624,000 adverse swing that is the largest single component of the $670,236,000 OCF decline (net income fell $235,433,000). TTM OCF then recovered to $1,982,033,000. (The maintenance OE variant prints $1,167,568,000 against the conservative $859,472,000, but that gap is a construction difference, not the working-capital effect: the maintenance formula — net income + D&A − capex capped at D&A − delta_nwc — itself subtracts the build, and the $308,096,000 by which it prints higher bridges exactly as a construction difference: starting from net income + D&A instead of operating cash flow contributes +$472,934,000, charging capex at D&A of $496,228,000 instead of the $680,802,000 actual +$184,574,000, no SBC deduction +$62,203,000, and the delta_nwc subtraction −$411,615,000. The working-capital conclusion above rests on the identified lines and the delta_nwc swing, not on the maintenance gap.) The year also contains real margin/demand erosion (operating income fell from $2,505,697,000 to $2,210,615,000 in the CSV history). The median is distorted upward: FY2024 ($12.20) and FY2025 ($12.05) predate the break. The TTM base ($11.06) sits between them and is the least stale of the three; the 0.90 base multiplier and the bear-weighted probabilities handle the remaining overstatement risk.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share range over the last 5 years spans >3x — $1.95 to $12.20 in the CSV): real, driven by the FY2023 inventory-glut OCF trough ($966,463,000 OCF that year) and the FY2024–25 peak. Handled by the TTM base plus 45% combined weight on the two bear scenarios.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag for the latest FY — net debt UNKNOWN, not zero): resolved from the filing — lululemon files no funded-debt tags because it carries no funded debt on the latest 10-K balance sheet; total liabilities are $3,494,903,000 (fundamentals.json), dominated by operating lease liabilities of $1,798,441,000, against cash of $1,807,202,000 and equity of $4,961,840,000. The engine's blank net debt is correct to print as unknown; the filing verdict is net cash before leases, roughly lease-neutral after them. No HIGH_NET_DEBT conclusion is drawn from the engine.
- **CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED** (only the combined cash + restricted-cash tag filed; net debt understated by any restricted amount): the combined tag is the filer's only cash presentation (fundamentals.json records the same basis: "includes restricted cash — no separate tag"), so the $1,807,202,000 cannot be split from the computed outputs. No leverage verdict in this analysis depends on the restricted portion being zero — the claim made is only that cash roughly covers lease liabilities, which holds for any plausible restricted amount at a retailer of this type; the exact restricted figure is a filing-note item the engine does not print, and it is stated here as unknown rather than assumed away.
- **SBC_TAG_RECONCILED** (Allocated exceeds Share for FY2019 +3.6%, FY2020 +1.1%, FY2021 +11.4%; the Allocated figure was used — key_numbers.md lists $29.6M / $46.1M / $56.6M used): confirmed as the engine's documented behaviour — the Share tag carried only part of stock compensation in those years and the larger Allocated figure is the conservative one. It touches none of the last 3 fiscal years and no TTM leg (all use ShareBasedCompensation: TTM SBC $91,231,000); a difference under 1% would be rounding, and the one year above that (FY2021, +11.4%) is five years outside the base window. No effect on the base or tier.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 2.4%/yr — share count CAGR −2.38%, key_numbers.md): diluted shares fell from 130,295,000 (FY2022) to 119,068,000 (latest FY) in the CSV, and buybacks continued into 2026 ($330.0M for 2.7M shares in Q2 FY2026 alone, company release). The engine credited +2.38pp inside its growth blend — but the final scenario starts were set directly from revenue prints and guidance (see the sanity check), replacing that blend, so the verdict does not double-count the buyback; if anything the shrinking count is uncredited support to per-share OE from here.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear-case tier D at 9.31% vs bull-case tier B at 15.36%): the verdict spans tiers by construction — this is a turnaround-or-fade coin weighted toward fade. Sized to the bear end throughout: the headline is the weighted Tier C, and the bear IV@15% of $55.31 is the figure a buyer should underwrite against, not the bull's $100.67.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The method range is the honest headline. On the engine's stale default blend (base growth +10.31%, TTM base, default probabilities) the same filing data printed Tier A at 20.46% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $146.01. On prints-and-guidance scenarios it prints Tier C at 11.72% with IV@15% of $72.45. The difference is the scenario inputs, not the data: the growth starts are the largest single change (base start +10.31% → 0.0%), but the bear-shifted probabilities (10/25/30/25/10 → 15/30/30/18/7) and the multiplier ladder (base 1.00 → 0.90, stripping the refund) each lower the weighted result independently, and this file does not decompose the split. What the three changes have in common is that they replace backward-looking defaults with the current prints and the guidance the company has actually given.
- What the price still assumes: at $97.76 the market is paying roughly the bull case (bull IV@15% $100.67) as its central expectation — i.e., that a CEO who has not yet presented a plan restores mid-single-digit growth on a refund-stripped OE base. That may happen; it is not the conservative end, and the sweep sizes to the conservative end.
- Quality is not the debate: 5/5 OE-positive years, SBC is small ($91,231,000 TTM against $1,982,033,000 TTM OCF), capex is a single clean filed line every year, no funded debt, and historical ROIC above 40% in every one of the last six years. The debate is purely whether the demand break is a product-cycle miss (fixable) or franchise erosion (not fixable on this timetable). Q2's breadth — leggings −20%, Americas comps −12%, China comps negative after a brand-sentiment incident — argues it is not one bad SKU.
- The balance sheet buys time, not growth: ~$1.8B cash against ~$1.8B of lease liabilities and no funded debt means no creditor forces the issue while O'Neill resets product; it also means there is no leverage distress discount in the price to harvest.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: C** (weighted IRR 11.72% on the final inputs; bear D 9.31% → bull B 15.36%)
- Confidence: **Low** (the base is filing-solid, but the forward path depends on an unpresented turnaround plan after a guidance reset that post-dates the TTM window, and the verdict spans three tiers across defensible scenario sets)
- One-liner: Premium athleisure brand, moat 5/10 and eroding — at $97.76 it does not clear 15% on reset numbers (weighted IRR 11.7%, weighted IV@15% $72.45; bear case 9.3%); it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$72.
